question: Does the Quezon flood-advisory label Catanauan correspond to an official source-named river in Catanauan, Quezon?
purpose: Cross-check the bare advisory label against primary hydrography and project sources while preserving uncertainty about the exact affected reach and keeping species evidence separate.

findings.evidence: Quezon Provincial Government General Flood Advisory No. 14, issued 7 August 2026, lists the bare label “Catanauan” among Quezon rivers and tributaries likely to be affected.

The BMB-DENR Atlas of Philippine Inland Wetlands and Classified Caves, Annex 2b, names Catanauan River in Catanauan, Quezon (map grid BS 85) and lists Tayabas Bay as outflow. Other atlas rows also place Bacong River, Canunbo River, and Dahican Creek in or partly in Catanauan.

DPWH Quezon III District Engineering Office bidding documents for Contract 25DM0076 name “Construction of Flood Control Structure along Catanauan River, Package B, Quezon” and give the location as Catanauan, Quezon.
supports: primary government project use of the Catanauan River name

crosswalk.resolutionLevel: official river-name and municipality-level crosswalk; exact advisory reach unresolved
crosswalk.confidence: Strong name/locality match: the official advisory uses Catanauan, the BMB-DENR atlas names Catanauan River in Catanauan and gives Tayabas Bay as outflow, and DPWH independently names Catanauan River at that locality. The atlas also lists other watercourses associated with Catanauan, so no exact reach is attributed.
crosswalk.mergeDecision: Add one separate source-named Catanauan River research lead. Link the advisory label at river-name/locality level, but do not infer the affected reach, channel route, or geometry.

reuseAndLimitations: The BMB atlas copyright terms permit educational or non-profit reproduction with acknowledgement; they are not an open license or public-app authorization. Only minimal factual source metadata is retained.
No item-specific open license or reuse terms were identified for the DPWH bid document or Quezon advisory.
The advisory is dated historical information, not a current warning. The crosswalk does not identify an exact affected reach or mapped river route.
No fish checklist, current presence/absence, salinity, water quality, access, fishing rule, or safety claim is established.
nextActions: Crosswalk the 18 remaining Quezon advisory labels against official hydrography or LGU sources.
Seek permitted route-scale hydrography before drawing or validating the Catanauan River course or advisory reach.
Review fish-specific evidence separately from the historical advisory and flood-control documents.
